title: MORI EP traffic
description: Expert-parallel dispatch / combine traffic. The kernel bandwidth of dispatch and combine (bytes of the tokens a kernel handled / the time the kernel ran: the number an EP benchmark reports), and, like the IO dashboard, which GPU sends how much to which over XGMI and what the GPUs put on each NIC over RDMA (payload over wall time).

list.name: host
list.label: Host
list.description: The GPUs and NICs of these hosts.

list.name: window
list.label: Average over
list.description: Window of the tiles and of the GPU to GPU matrices. The charts over time follow the dashboard's own resolution. 5s and 10s are for the millisecond data source: scraped data has a point every few seconds.

panels.title: Dispatch bandwidth
panels.description: Bytes of the tokens a rank's experts got (dispatch) or gave back (combine), tokens that stay on the GPU included, divided by the time the kernel ran, measured on the device. This is the bandwidth an EP benchmark reports (bytes received / kernel time; the inter-node benchmark calls it the XGMI bandwidth); it does not depend on how often EP is called. Only kernels that are timed have it. Tile: all selected ranks together (total bytes / total kernel time).

panels.title: XGMI sent per GPU
panels.description: EP payload bytes per second one GPU sends over XGMI, to all its peers together, dispatch and combine: the average over the GPUs of the selected hosts that send, and over the window. Per second of wall time, not of kernel time: it follows how often EP is called and stays far below the kernel bandwidth when the GPUs spend most of their time outside EP.

panels.title: RDMA sent per NIC
panels.description: Bytes per second one NIC sends for the GPUs' own RDMA (EP payload with its headers and signals): the average over the NICs of the selected hosts that send, and over the window. No data when EP runs inside one node. Per second of wall time, not of kernel time: it follows how often EP is called and stays far below the kernel bandwidth when the GPUs spend most of their time outside EP.

panels.title: Data age
panels.description: Seconds since the newest sample of the selected hosts' ranks. A few seconds: the processes are reporting, and a chart at zero means no traffic. Growing, or no data: nothing is reporting (the load ended, or the scrape or the push broke), and the charts say nothing about the traffic.

panels.title: Kernel bandwidth of dispatch / combine (bytes / kernel time)
Kernel bandwidth by operation
panels.description: Bytes of the tokens a rank's experts got (dispatch) or gave back (combine), tokens that stay on the GPU included, divided by the time the kernel ran, measured on the device. This is the bandwidth an EP benchmark reports (bytes received / kernel time; the inter-node benchmark calls it the XGMI bandwidth); it does not depend on how often EP is called. Only kernels that are timed have it. One line per operation, all selected ranks together. Dashed, inter-node kernels only: the RDMA hop, the bytes the ranks put on RDMA for other nodes over the same kernel time. (The inter-node benchmark's RDMA bandwidth also counts a token's own node as a destination: with N nodes and balanced routing it reads N / (N - 1) times this.)

sum by (op) (rate(mori_ep_rdma_bytes_total{host=~"$host",impl=~"$impl",direction="tx"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (op) (rate(mori_ep_kernel_seconds_total{host=~"$host",impl=~"$impl"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host, gpu, rank, impl, op) sum by (host, gpu, rank, impl, op) (rate(mori_ep_rdma_bytes_total{host=~"$host",impl=~"$impl",direction="tx"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: $mhost: GPU to GPU over XGMI, rate (sender -> receiver), average over $window
panels.description: EP payload bytes per second between the GPUs of this host, dispatch and combine together. A cell is the rate and its direction: "6.2 GB/s (4 -> 5)" is what GPU 4 sent to GPU 5. The row is the sender, the column the receiver. The diagonal is empty: tokens that stay on a GPU do not cross XGMI. Stronger blue: 10 GB/s and more; weaker: 1 to 10 GB/s; faint: less. Payload, not link bytes. Per second of wall time, not of kernel time: it follows how often EP is called and stays far below the kernel bandwidth when the GPUs spend most of their time outside EP.

targets.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(count_values by (gpu, peer_gpu) ("rate", round((sum by (gpu, peer_gpu) (rate(mori_ep_xgmi_bytes_total{host="${mhost:raw}",impl=~"$impl",direction="tx"}[$window])) >= 1e9) / 1e8)), "rate", "0.$1", "rate", "(\\d)"), "rate", "$1.$2", "rate", "(\\d+)(\\d)"), "unit", "GB/s", "", "") or label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(count_values by (gpu, peer_gpu) ("rate", round((sum by (gpu, peer_gpu) (rate(mori_ep_xgmi_bytes_total{host="${mhost:raw}",impl=~"$impl",direction="tx"}[$window])) < 1e9 >= 5e4) / 1e5)), "rate", "0.$1", "rate", "(\\d)"), "rate", "$1.$2", "rate", "(\\d+)(\\d)"), "unit", "MB/s", "", ""), "tmp", "|", "rate", "unit", "gpu", "peer_gpu"), "cell", "$1 $2 ($3 -> $4)", "tmp", "(.*)\\|(.*)\\|(.*)\\|(.*)")

panels.title: Sent per GPU over XGMI
panels.description: EP payload bytes per second each GPU of the selected hosts sent over XGMI, to all its peers together, dispatch and combine. Per second of wall time, not of kernel time: it follows how often EP is called and stays far below the kernel bandwidth when the GPUs spend most of their time outside EP.

panels.title: Received per GPU over XGMI
panels.description: EP payload bytes per second each GPU of the selected hosts received over XGMI, from all its peers together.

panels.title: Sent per NIC
panels.description: Bytes per second the GPUs themselves put on RDMA (IBGDA), by the NIC of the selected hosts that sent them. Everything a rank's kernels send to another node goes through here: EP payload plus its headers and signals. This is the number to hold against the NIC's own transmit counter (equal to the byte on an RoCE NIC; an InfiniBand counter adds about 1 % of packet headers). A NIC has the colour of the GPU with the same index. No data when EP runs inside one node.

panels.title: Received per NIC
panels.description: Bytes per second of the GPUs' own RDMA, by the NIC of the selected hosts that received them.
